title: Learning to Compare Neural Representations from Parameterized Computation Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2611.26081v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Comparing internal representations across trained models is important for identifying corresponding layers and selecting components for model reuse. Yet, direct comparisons at inference require evaluating candidate models on known reference inputs and collecting their internal activations. In this paper, we study whether internal representation similarity measured across independently trained models can instead be learned to predict in unseen models from their parameterized computations. We introduce a framework that applies a graph metanetwork for mapping each internal site to an embedding derived from its upstream computations while accounting for hidden-coordinate permutation and internal attention-basis transformations. translated_title: 从参数化计算图中学习比较神经表示
translated_abstract: 比较已训练模型的内部表示对于识别对应层以及为模型重用选择组件非常重要。然而，在推理时进行直接比较需要在已知参考输入上评估候选模型并收集其内部激活。本文研究了能否通过学习，从模型的参数化计算中直接预测内部表示的相似性，从而在未见过的模型上进行推断，而无需在独立训练的模型之间实际测量相似性。我们提出了一个应用图元网络的框架，将每个内部位置映射到由其上游计算导出的嵌入，同时考虑隐藏坐标排列和内部注意力基变换。我们分析了所提估计器的结构特性，并推导了层检索与拼接候选选择的条件性保证。实验表明，学习到的预测器能够支持表示关系的估计。
tldr: 提出了一种基于图元网络的框架，可直接从模型的参数化计算图中学习预测内部表示相似性，无需实际运行模型即可实现层检索与模型拼接组件选择。
en_tdlr: Proposes a graph metanetwork framework that learns to predict internal representation similarity directly from parameterized computation graphs, enabling layer retrieval and stitching candidate selection without actually running the models.
